products.name: Freepik AI
products.note: Stock image AI generation; commercial licensing; EU-hosted; content moderation

reading.body:
Freepik's only listed AI product is an image and graphic design tool, and the data records no compute, data center, or power details for the company at all.

The profile is thin by design. It names one product, Freepik AI, and attaches four attributes: stock image generation, commercial licensing, EU hosting, and content moderation. Those attributes describe a service layer, not infrastructure. Nothing here says where the models run, how large they are, or what they cost to serve.

For AI scaling, the relevant fact is the EU hosting note. It places at least part of the serving footprint inside Europe, which ties the product to European grid and data center capacity rather than to any single hyperscaler region. The data does not say whether that hosting is owned, colocated, or rented, so no conclusion about power draw follows.

What this record cannot support is any claim about Freepik's compute demand, model size, or growth. It is a company entry with one product and a refresh interval of 90 days, and it should be read as a pointer to a service, not as evidence about the buildings and power behind it.
